To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of fluvoxamine in a patient with Tourette's syndrome and obsessive-compulsive (OCD) disorder led to worsening of both the OCD and Tourette symptoms.
Fluvoxamine worsens tics, leads to coprolalia and does not help OCD.
fluvoxamine and the dopamine antagonist pimozide, when combined, may be an effective treatment for OCD in patients with Tourette's syndrome.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of fluvoxamine and pimazide was effective for the treatment of concurrent OCD and Tourette’s syndrome.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single treatment for Tourette’s syndrome.
